title: Seat liveness leaf: a silence-vs-absolute-cap decider and a Windows process-tree/CPU probe, where an unobservable seat is never killed for silence
description:
LEAF split out of task-8f653d86bb4f445cb7ee358c5559f99a ("The seat timeout is a wall-clock cap from spawn, not a liveness test") by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18, because the whole fix measured at 11 files against the 10-file cap. That row is the CONSUMER and declares dependsOn on this one; it wires what this row builds into agent-spawner.ts, adds the absolute-cap knob, the moe start env roster and the docs. THIS row lands a pure module and its tests only, and touches no existing production file.

WHY IT EXISTS (measured live on UnAI 2026-09-18, and at HEAD). agent-spawner.ts:399-402 arms `setTimeout(beginTermination, timeoutMs)` once at spawn and never rearms it, so a seat is killed at MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS however busy it is. The quiet notice at :404-414 cannot help: the seat is `claude -p` WITHOUT --output-format, which writes nothing until it finishes, so every seat shows "0 bytes seen" for its whole life. Node 5 (15f56b77) was at minute 26 with a live bash.exe tool child started 60 s earlier (claude.exe cpu 25 s) and was on course to be killed at minute 30 mid-work.

WHY NOT STREAM OUTPUT INSTEAD. The parent row allows either streaming (`--output-format stream-json`) or a process probe. Streaming is REJECTED: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-exit-classifier.ts pattern-matches the seat's TEXT to detect provider limits, with regexes measured against specific claude.exe builds (`/You've hit your usage limit(?![.\w])/iu`, the 429 banner), and its own comment at :58 warns that a seat printing "rate limit" inside its JSON output must NOT park the provider. Routing everything the model says through JSON events risks a seat whose model merely writes "rate limit" in a code comment falsely pausing the whole fleet's provider. A process probe changes no output format and leaves the classifier untouched.

THE TWO LOAD-BEARING FACTS the design must honour:
1. THE SEAT ROOT IS A SHELL, NOT THE PROVIDER. On Windows the seat is spawned through cmd.exe (governor observed cmd pid 49960 -> claude.exe 17324). So "a live descendant exists", measured from the spawned pid, is ALWAYS true while the seat runs, because the provider process itself is that descendant. A tool child must be counted STRICTLY BELOW the provider process. CPU progress summed over the whole tree is the more robust signal and must be honoured independently.
2. ONLY POSITIVELY OBSERVED SILENCE MAY KILL (epic rail 4: unverifiable evidence gains no authority). A probe that fails, times out, or has no implementation for the platform reports UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN never earns a silence kill; only the absolute cap applies then. Without this rule, silent `claude -p` seats on any platform without a probe would be killed SOONER than today.

CONTRACT this row must export (the consumer row plans against these exact names; changing them requires amending task-8f653d86):
- `SeatLivenessSample` = { kind: "OBSERVED"; cpuMs: number; toolChildren: readonly { pid: number; command: string }[] } | { kind: "UNKNOWN"; reason: string }
- `SeatProbe` = (seatPid: number) => Promise<SeatLivenessSample>
- `SeatLivenessVerdict` = { kind: "CONTINUE" } | { kind: "KILL_SILENT"; silentMs: number; lastActivity: string | null } | { kind: "KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP"; ageMs: number; lastActivity: string | null }
- `createSeatLivenessTracker({ startedAtMs, silenceMs, maxRuntimeMs })` returning { noteOutput(nowMs), noteSample(nowMs, sample), verdict(nowMs) } — ALL liveness state lives here so the 480-line spawner stays thin.
- `createWindowsSeatProbe(run?: RuntimeCommand)` — one Get-CimInstance Win32_Process query per call behind an injectable runner, following apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-broker-identity.ts:14/:38 (the `RuntimeCommand` seam and `runPowerShell`).

OUT OF SCOPE: agent-spawner.ts, the knobs, the env roster, the docs (task-8f653d86 owns them); a POSIX probe (follow-up — on a platform with no probe a stuck seat now lives until the absolute cap instead of 30 min, which is the deliberate cost of never killing a seat on unverifiable evidence).
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts exports the exact contract named in the description (SeatLivenessSample, SeatProbe, SeatLivenessVerdict, createSeatLivenessTracker, createWindowsSeatProbe) with its one-line .js bridge beside it, and the file stays at or under 250 lines.

The tracker never returns KILL_SILENT unless silence was POSITIVELY observed: an arm feeds only UNKNOWN samples past the silence window and asserts verdict kind CONTINUE, then past the absolute cap asserts KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP; a second arm feeds OBSERVED samples with no CPU progress, no tool child and no output past the window and asserts KILL_SILENT with the exact silentMs. Reason codes asserted by value, never merely 'not CONTINUE'.

Each liveness signal is honoured INDEPENDENTLY, one arm per signal: output alone, a tool child alone (CPU flat), and CPU progress alone (no tool child) each keep the verdict CONTINUE past the silence window. The tool-child arm uses a tree where the only descendants are the shell and the provider process and asserts that does NOT count as a tool child.

The Windows probe is driven through its injectable runner in tests (no real process needed): a well-formed CIM answer yields OBSERVED with the summed CPU and the tool children below the provider; a failing, empty, malformed or timed-out runner yields UNKNOWN with a named reason, never OBSERVED and never a throw. One real-host arm, gated like apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts, probes the test runner's own pid on Windows and asserts OBSERVED.

Gate quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.test.ts`, plus `pnpm typecheck` (the daemon project now carries erasableSyntaxOnly, so the new module must be erasable).

implementationPlan.description:
CALIBRATE. Re-measure both CPU bands ON THIS HOST through the PRODUCTION probe, so the floor comes from a measurement, as governor ruling msg-54bb4cb0 requires. Work only in %TEMP%/moe-task-eca3780d-<yourWorkerId>/ and write nothing to the repo.

Write a small .mjs that does three things:
- imports `createSeatActivityProbe` from the landed apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness-probe.ts by file URL (the daemon graph is erasable, and node 24 strips the types);
- spawns the seat the way the win32 spawner does: a command LINE with `shell: true`, so the root is cmd.exe;
- every 60 s, records the probe's {cpuMs, descendants} for the ROOT pid. That is the same tree sum production judges.
The prior worker's scripts are still in %TEMP%/moe-task-eca3780d-worker-e0435164/. hung.mjs there is the fake-API recipe.

(i) HUNG band, at least 10 one-minute intervals. Run a real `claude -p --setting-sources "" --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --tools Read` against a localhost fake API that accepts POST /v1/messages and never answers. Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>, a dummy ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1. The recipe is in Serena memory gotcha-seat-liveness-cpu-calibration-hung-claude-is-not-idle. This costs nothing, and nothing leaves the host.

(ii) WORKING band, at least 10 one-minute intervals with NO tool child, meaning descendants equal the chain the first sample saw. Use a real `claude -p` with the same flags but `--tools Read,Glob,Grep`.
- Those tools run in-process, so no child process appears. `--setting-sources ""` and `--strict-mcp-config` also keep hook and MCP-server processes out of the tree.
- Give it work that keeps the model streaming for several minutes, for example reading and explaining three large files of this repo in detail.
- If one run is too short, repeat it. Drop the interval that contains the process exit.
- The whole cost is a few minutes of real model time.
- Do NOT sample an interactive TUI claude session. Its rendering adds CPU that a -p seat does not have, and the prior working figures may carry that bias.
- The two bands may run at the same time.

(iii) DECIDE the floor as a RATE: ms of tree CPU per minute of wall clock. The margin that matters is the one above the hung band. A single crossing resets a hung seat's silence clock, so the floor must exceed EVERY hung interval. A working seat needs only one crossing per 20-minute window. Apply this rule:
- If 1.5 x max(hung) <= min(working), the floor is the geometric midpoint of max(hung) and min(working), rounded.
- Otherwise, the floor is 1.5 x max(hung), rounded up, provided that is still below the working MEDIAN. Say so in the comment.
- If even that fails, STOP and moe.report_blocked to the governor with both full lists. CPU then cannot tell hung from working per interval on this host, and deciding which failure to accept is not this row's call.

Prior figures from the same host (worker-e0435164), in ms per 60 s: hung 156, 328, 109, 172; working 766, 859, 781, 1578; idle node 0-31. They gave a floor of about 500.

In the step note, record every interval of both bands, the rule branch applied and the chosen value. If that would exceed ~4500 chars, put the lists in a row comment and cite its id, because step notes truncate silently at 5000.
Kill every process you spawned, and prove none survive with a Get-CimInstance Win32_Process query on those pids.

RED: the unit arms in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.test.ts. Every arm asserts by value. Use toEqual on whole tick objects wherever the landed file already does.

CORRECTION 1: an unobserved tick is not silence.
(1) FLIP and retitle "carries the probe's own reason when it fails or throws, and grants no liveness for it" (:98).
- The {ok:false} tick and the throwing tick both now answer silentMs 0. detail and probeFailure are unchanged.
- lastActivity() stays "seat start at 13:12:04Z", because an unobserved tick is neither activity nor silence. Rewrite the :123 FAIL-CLOSED comment to say so.
- Add one more failed tick past the window, at +21 min, that still answers silentMs 0.
(2) FLIP and retitle "says so when there is no probe, and judges on output alone" (:88): silentMs is 0 on every tick, and detail stays "no output; no activity probe".
Make the same flip in "does not probe a seat without a pid" (:150). Its clock is pinned at T0 today, so ADVANCE it 60 s before the tick. Otherwise silentMs 0 holds by construction and the flip proves nothing.
(3) NEW arm, "one unobserved tick mid-silence restarts the observed-silence count at that tick":
- observed flat ticks at +1 to +5 min answer silentMs 60_000 to 300_000;
- a failed tick at +6 min answers silentMs 0;
- the observed flat ticks after it count from +6 min, so at +26 min silentMs is 1_200_000;
- stillness() ends "since 13:18:04Z", while lastActivity() still reads "seat start at 13:12:04Z".

CORRECTION 2: the CPU floor is a rate.
(4) NEW arm, "the CPU floor is a rate":
- expect(CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS_PER_MINUTE).toBe(<step-2 value>);
- over a 60 s interval, a delta of floor-1 reads "cpu unchanged" and silentMs grows, while a delta equal to the floor reads "cpu +..." and silentMs is 0;
- over a 120 s interval (one failed tick between two observed ticks), 2*floor-1 reads unchanged and 2*floor counts as activity;
- two observed samples at the same instant never read as progress.
(5) NEW arm, "the floor separates the bands measured on this host":
- the step-2 hung maximum per 60 s reads "cpu unchanged";
- the step-2 working minimum per 60 s counts as activity.
Copy the literals from the step-2 record and name that record in a comment. This pins the constant to the measurement, not only to itself.
(6) REPLACE the old arm "calls CPU growth at or above the floor activity, and growth below it unchanged" (:62), with its per-tick 249/1_300 literals, with arm (4).
(7) NEW real-host arm (DoD 4), gated like apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts:54:
- `const REAL = process.env.MOE_SEAT_PROBE_REAL === "1"` and `it.runIf(REAL)`;
- build createSeatLiveness({ now: () => Date.now(), pid: process.pid, probe: createSeatActivityProbe() });
- the awaited tick's detail contains "cpu baseline taken" and does NOT contain "tree unobserved", and probeFailure is undefined.
No real-host arm exists yet: seat-liveness-probe.test.ts has no runIf.

Leave every other landed arm unchanged. The launcher-chain arm (:39), the output arm (:76) and the async rebase arm (:127) stay green under both corrections.
Run the file and CONFIRM that arms (1) through (5) are RED before step 4. Quote the failing assertions.

GREEN, in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts only.

CORRECTION 1:
- Add `let lastUnobservedAt = startedAt;`.
- In settle(), two branches set `lastUnobservedAt = at`: the no-probe branch (answer undefined, which also covers pid undefined) and the isProbeFailure branch.
- The returned silentMs becomes `at - Math.max(lastActivityAt, lastUnobservedAt)`. stillness() reports `since` that same instant, so the kill line's "silent Xm" and its "since" agree.
- lastActivity() is unchanged, so the absolute-cap line still names the real last activity.
- Three docs state the old rule: the FAIL-CLOSED comment (:122), the `probe` option doc (:48, "Absent means the wrapper judges on output alone") and the SeatLivenessTick.probeFailure doc (:56-57, "No liveness was granted for it"). Replace them with the new rule and its reasons:
  - a silence kill needs a whole window of POSITIVELY observed stillness;
  - a tick that could not see the tree is not evidence of silence (epic rail 4: unverifiable evidence gains no authority), so it restarts the count;
  - be honest about the limits: a probe that fails on every tick leaves only the absolute cap; one transient failure delays a kill by at most one window; a probe that fails at least once in every window also leaves only the cap.
- The header sentence at :16-18 says a seat with a tool child at every tick is "judged on CPU growth and output alone". That describes the launcher-chain blind spot, and it is still true, so leave it.

CORRECTION 2:
- Rename CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS to CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS_PER_MINUTE = <step-2 value>.
- Delete the `cpuActivityFloorMs` option. The step-1 census found no caller anywhere, and keeping it would let a caller pass a per-tick number into a per-minute comparison.
- Keep `previousCpuAt` beside previousCpuMs. Count progress iff `elapsed > 0 && cpuDelta * 60_000 >= floor * elapsed`.
- Compare by multiplication, never by division. Windows cpuMs is fractional (multiples of 15.625 ms), and these products stay exact because they are far below 2^53.
- A negative delta keeps its landed meaning: a process left the tree. It counts as activity, and the baseline is rebased.
- Rebase the baseline (both the ms and the instant) on every OBSERVED sample, and never on an unobserved one. The next delta then spans the gap, and the rate normalises it.
- Replace the UNMEASURED comment (:23-41) with the calibration record: date, host, method (the production probe, one CIM query per 60 s), both interval lists, the idle reference, the rule branch and the chosen value. Keep the re-calibration recipe short.
- Keep these labels unchanged: "cpu +N.Ns", "cpu unchanged", "cpu rebased (a process left the tree)" and "cpu baseline taken".

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. A PER-TICK FLOOR WITH A NEW VALUE vs a RATE. The rate was chosen. The landed tick runs every min(quietNoticeMs || 60 s, silenceMs). An unobserved tick, or a tick skipped by the probing guard, stretches the interval between two observed samples. A per-tick floor silently changes its meaning whenever the cadence changes; a rate (cpuDelta * 60_000 >= floor * elapsed) does not.
2. MARK AN UNOBSERVED TICK AS ACTIVITY (set lastActivityAt) vs a SEPARATE lastUnobservedAt ANCHOR. The separate anchor was chosen. Otherwise lastActivity() would name 'tree unobserved' as the seat's last activity in the absolute-cap line, which is false.
3. CARRY OBSERVED SILENCE ACROSS AN UNOBSERVED GAP (using the CPU delta that spans it) vs RESTART THE COUNT. Restart was chosen. The CPU delta does cover the gap, but a tool child that burns no CPU while it sleeps or waits on the network is invisible inside it, and rule 2 forbids counting what was not seen.
4. AVERAGE CPU OVER THE WHOLE WINDOW instead of per interval. This would discriminate better, but it is a redesign beyond the two named corrections (ruling msg-54bb4cb0: 'two named corrections, not a rewrite'). It is the fallback if step 2 finds the bands overlapping, which is why step 2 blocks in that case instead of picking a side.
5. THE WORKER BRINGS MAIN IN ITSELF (a merge, a cherry-pick of 4eb87ec4, or `git checkout origin/main -- files`). Rejected: a merge is a whole-tree commit, a partial import drags in other rows' hunks, and creating the files is the add/add duplicate the ruling forbids.
